sections.skill: Separate money raised from profit and compute runway

questions.prompt: Is a 30,000-dollar loan profit?

choices.text: Yes, all cash received is profit
Yes, if spent within a month
Only if the bank is local

questions.intro: Cash received is not automatically PROFIT. Loans and money from owners or investors are FINANCING: loans must be repaid, and investors own part of the business. Grants and crowdfunding must be classified by their terms; reward crowdfunding backers, for example, are owed the promised products. PROFIT = recognized income minus expenses; for most small businesses it comes from selling for more than costs. A business can raise a lot of money and still lose money on every sale. Track BURN RATE (how much cash the business uses each month) and RUNWAY (months until cash runs out = cash / monthly burn).

questions.prompt: 15,000 cash, 3,000 burn. What is the runway?
questions.intro: Runway = cash / monthly burn. Example: 18,000 cash with 2,000 burned per month gives 18,000 / 2,000 = 9 months. If the result is not whole, round DOWN, because a partial month of cash will not cover a full month: 10,000 / 3,000 = 3.33, so about 3 full months. If burn rises, runway falls; if burn drops, runway grows.
